AK-2025-HB39.aiSummary: The bill became law and applies to public school students in Alaska who are deaf or hard of hearing, or may be. It requires school districts to give parents clear information about hearing tools, ways to communicate, and related services, and to follow the parent’s chosen communication method when providing services. It also directs the state to support one or more programs for deaf students, including possible residential services, and sets rules for school districts that run such programs.

AK-2025-HB278.aiSummary: The bill would create the Alaska-Ireland Trade Commission in the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development. The group would have five governor appointees, two House members, and two Senate members, and it would work on trade, investment, business, research, and school exchanges between Alaska and Ireland. It would also set meeting rules, reporting duties, and allow grants or gifts to help pay some costs; the act would take effect right away.

AK-2025-HB25.aiSummary: The bill would bar restaurants from serving prepared food in polystyrene foam food containers, and it would also stop the state from using or buying them. It would let customers bring clean containers for food if state rules set steps to avoid cross-contamination, and it would allow some exceptions for outside-the-state food, disaster areas, and local rules. It would take effect on January 1, 2027, and it was later vetoed by the governor.

AK-2025-HB117.aiSummary: The law lets Alaska require electronic monitoring on certain state commercial finfish trawl boats, but only if the boats already have the needed gear for a federal fishery and no extra cost is shifted to fishers.
